decisions.reason: As a close-to-core handle line in a growing market, it is inexpensive for a large broad-range supplier to keep this option open while adoption across projects becomes clearer.
This handle family fits the firm's established assortment and customer base, so the firm would likely retain it at least another year because the downside of waiting is limited.
A single new handle design is somewhat easier to prune than a whole family, but after only about a year the firm still has reason to wait for market feedback from architects and projects.
Because it is an incremental design close to the firm's core offer, management would usually continue it unless results were clearly poor, which is not shown here.
This product family extends the firm's breadth in a familiar category, and keeping it preserves option value with relatively modest ongoing commitment.

As a flagship electronic access system aligned with the firm's digital direction, its strategic upside and still-unresolved uncertainty make early withdrawal unlikely despite somewhat higher carrying costs.
